main_text.p: affeveratione aut obteftatione, fortiùs adhuc obliget:omnium tamen fortiffimè obligat votū,quod ipsi Deo nuncupatur, [illegible, ~2 letters]& Juramentum quod homini sed Deo tamen tefte præftatur.Obligat ergo omne Juramentū conscientiam;tam Afferto-rium, quàm Promissorium. De Promissorio, quandoquidem tempus futurum respicit, nulli poteft esse dubium: sed de Assertorio fortassis non sine [illegible, ~3 letters]ratione dubitari posset ex eo, quòd omnis Obligatio est ad aliquod futurum; di-ctum autem sit prius Assertorii juramen-ti à Promissorio discrimen in hoc con-sistere, quòd illud rem præsentem vel [illegible, ~2 letters]præteritam respiceret , hoc futuram. Sed facilis est solutio. Nimirum juramenti quà tale Obligatio non cadit pri-mario super Objectum, sive Materiam juramenti; sic enim Assertorium jura-mentum, cujus objectum est res præ-terita aut præsens, non posset obligati-onem de futuro inducere: sed obligatio cadit immediatè & directè super Sub-jectum, hoc est conscientiam jurantis, qui in utraque Juramenti specie tenetur ad aliquod officium de futuro præ-stan-dum.
[Marginal notes at the right edge are cut off by the scan; their text is not legible.]

page.notes: The right-edge margin shows several cut-off fragments of marginal notes (about twenty short pieces, for example "li", "ci", "ju", "qu", "ar", "tr", "o", "p", "te") that cannot be read beyond their first letters; the placement of the marked notes is approximate. The heading word "SECT." at the bottom right is cut off by the scan edge. The "Juramentū" and "votū" macrons are read from a small scan and may be doubtful. The text "Sect" is a catchword, not a heading.
